descriptionChirho: Describing something living that has lost its moisture and vitality; used of a man's withered hand (Matt 12:10, Mark 3:1,3, Luke 6:6,8) and of dried-up vegetation or trees (Matt 21:19-20). The multilingual translations confirm a biological/organic drying: arb يَابِسِينَ 'dried out (of persons/limbs)', kor 마른 'withered/dried', swa waliokauka 'those who have dried up' / umekauka 'has dried up', spa seca/secos 'dry/withered', hin सूखा 'dried up'.

Describing land or terrain that is arid, lacking water; used of dry land as opposed to the sea (Matt 23:15, Heb 11:29) and of dry or parched conditions. The multilingual evidence shows a geographic/physical sense: arb يَابِسَة 'dry (land)', kor 마른-땅-을 'dry land (accusative)', swa kavu 'dry/arid', spa tierra-seca 'dry land', hin सूखी 'dry (feminine)'. Distinguished from the 'withered' sense by applying to inorganic terrain rather than living organisms.
